references.text: Parallel text about the sign on the hand and the mark between the eyes, recalling the Lord's deliverance from Egypt.
Moses repeats the command to bind the Lord's words as a sign on the hand and have them as a mark on the forehead.
Another repetition of the command to bind the words as a sign on the hand and a mark between the eyes.
Proverbs advises binding parents' commands to the heart and tying them around the neck, echoing this command.
Encouragement to bind wisdom to the fingers and write it on the tablet of the heart.
Reference to the Lord's strong hand that was to force Pharaoh to let the Israelites go out.
Description of how the Lord brought Israel out of Egypt with a strong hand.
The Israelites' confession that the Lord brought them out of Egypt with a strong hand.
The command that the book of the law shall not depart from the mouth, parallel to the Lord's law being in the mouth.
Jesus notes that the Pharisees make their prayer straps broad, based on the literal interpretation of this verse.
Highlights the connection between remembering the exodus and ethical demands for treating foreigners.
Prophetic use of exodus language to affirm God's power to save in new times.
Expands the concept of 'sign' from a national memory to a universal act of salvation for all peoples.
Links the memory of the exodus to the theological purpose: to know God.
Demonstrates how the memory of the exodus is the foundation for keeping God's commands (here, the Sabbath).
